title: Ar-Rahim, the Especially Merciful
hook: the Especially Merciful, mercy close to each one, shaped like a family
tomorrow: if mercy is that close, who's actually in charge here?

segments.voice: Yesterday, Ar-Rahman: one part of mercy sent down, and a mare lifting her hoof. Mercy for all. Today, the name that walks beside it.

A hospital is full of care, and still it's the one nurse who learned your name that you remember. A kindness the size of a crowd is easy to miss. So, yesterday's question: does mercy that big ever find just one person? Bismillah ar-Rahman ar-Rahim. Same root, two names, side by side. The second is Ar-Rahim.
screen: `THE NURSE WHO LEARNED YOUR NAME.` → `SAME ROOT, TWO NAMES.` → `AR-RAHIM.`

segments.voice: Scholars have explained the pair this way: Ar-Rahman is mercy as wide as creation; Ar-Rahim is mercy that keeps arriving, close, to this one. The Qur'an says in Surah al-Ahzab, in Pickthall's words: He is ever Merciful to the believers. And a sacred hadith in Abu Dawud and Tirmidhi brings it all the way home. In paraphrase, Allah says: I am ar-Rahman. I created the rahim, the womb and the ties of family, and gave it a name from My own name. Whoever keeps those ties, I keep him. So the closest mercy has the shape of a family: the aunt who calls, the cousin you stopped texting. Now a neighbor who says something close. In the Torah, when God passes before Moses, the words in the 1917 Jewish translation are: The LORD, the LORD, God, merciful and gracious, long-suffering, and abundant in goodness and truth. Jewish prayer books set those words in prayers for forgiveness. What's shared: a God described first by mercy, close enough to meet one person. An honest difference: Muslims meet that mercy as names of Allah, said at the opening of the surahs; Jews meet it as a scene in the Torah, God's own words to Moses on the mountain. Something to tell a friend tonight: in this sacred hadith, the word for family ties is named after mercy.
screen: `WIDE, AND CLOSE.` · `THE RAHIM, NAMED FROM HIS NAME.` · `A NEIGHBOR: MERCIFUL AND GRACIOUS.` · `SHARED, AND HONESTLY DIFFERENT.` · then, large: `MERCY FOR ME.`

segments.voice: Bring to mind one person in your family, by blood or by choice, where the tie has worn thin. Decide one small mercy for them, a call or a message or a favor, and when it could happen. For the sit, hold their face in mind and let the plan settle.
screen: `ONE THIN TIE.` · `ONE SMALL MERCY, AND WHEN.`
